title: preprocess-file
summary: Diagnostic that prints a file's {$IFDEF}-resolved source to stdout under a given define set
intro: Read this when you need to see what the preprocessor makes of a file. It prints the IFDEF-resolved source under the defines you give it, without running a full compile; it is a diagnostic, not a daily tool.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint preprocess-file --in PATH [--define SYM]... [--numeric K=V]... [--include-mode off|defines-only] [--no-near-search] [--tolerances] [--include-sites] (diagnostic: print {$IFDEF}-resolved source to stdout)
help: drag-lint preprocess-file --in PATH [--define SYM]... [--numeric K=V]... [--include-mode off|defines-only] [--no-near-search] [--tolerances] [--include-sites]   (diagnostic: print {$IFDEF}-resolved source to stdout)

questions.ask: What does this file look like after IFDEF resolution?
What if I define a symbol?
Which include files did this file pull in, and what did each contribute?
